bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing customer relationships in the Structured Copper LAN Cable segment, supported by commitment to customer service excellence and prompt delivery, widely appreciated by leading clients
- Diversified product portfolio across Optical Fibre Cables, Copper Telecommunication Cables, Structured Copper LAN Cables and Specialty cables, which allowed the Company to offset a severe OFC industry downturn with strong LAN cable volumes
- Focus on setting industry benchmark standards in the Structured Copper LAN Cable segment
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Structural technology substitution away from copper cables — All telecom operators are increasingly going for optical fibre cables, meaning traditional copper telecommunication cable requirements in the network are no longer required, structurally reducing that product line's addressable demand.
- Intense, price-led competition eroding margins — Cut-throat competition is described as the norm in the cable industry, with some players offering highly advantageous price levels that bring margins under huge pressure.
- Inferior-technology competition affecting network standards — Players offering products with inferior technology can affect network standards, pulling the industry away from international benchmarks.
- Customer concentration and credit risk — The Company flags a highly concentrated customer base as a financial risk; credit risk could increase if the financial condition of the Company's customers declines.
- Raw material / commodity price volatility — Adverse movements in raw material prices are cited among the Company's financial risks, which can compress margins given input-cost sensitivity.
- Foreign exchange exposure — The Company is exposed to foreign exchange volatility and related exchange-rate fluctuations, relevant given its export sales of Optical Fibre Cables.
- Low capacity utilisation and un-remunerative pricing — Financial risks explicitly include low-capacity utilisation and un-remunerative prices, alongside shorter delivery schedules and exposure to liquidated damages.
- Logistics and geopolitical disruption — Sourcing raw materials and distributing finished products face logistics bottlenecks; recent geopolitical disturbances and rising transportation costs have further intensified this challenge.

outlook.body: The Company added Rs 191.05 lakhs to fixed assets during FY 2025-26, mainly on expansion of its existing manufacturing capacity. Separately, the Board approved a Scheme of Amalgamation with Vindhya Telelinks Limited (appointed date April 1, 2026) intended, among other things, to consolidate the manufacturing capabilities and capacities of both companies into a larger unified entity with enhanced market presence and improved competitive positioning for larger, capital-intensive multi-state infrastructure projects.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for Optical Fibre Cables has shown signs of revival since late March 2026 and is expected to strengthen in FY 2026-27
- India's telecom sector is expected to sustain strong growth momentum in FY 2026-27, driven by rapid 5G adoption, increasing fiberisation, and rising data consumption
- Union Budget 2026-27 allocated Rs 74,000 crore to the Department of Telecommunications for infrastructure revival and BSNL's 4G/5G Advanced rollouts, expected to drive large-scale fiberisation of telecom towers and backhaul networks
- Rising investments in data centres are accelerating demand for specialised telecom and data cables
- The Indian wire and cable industry is projected to grow at a CAGR of 11-13% through FY 2029
- FY 2026-27 has begun on a strong note for the global Optical Fibre Cable business, with both demand and pricing reaching record levels, led by North America and Europe hyperscale data-centre build-outs
- Revenue growth in FY 2025-26 was primarily driven by a significant rise in Structured LAN Cable sales, while order flow for Optical Fibre Cables remained broadly in line with the previous year
- The order flow for Optical Fibre Cables remained broadly in line with the previous year
